summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A)

## BOOK 1 — "My Shipmate Louise: The Romance of a Wreck" (W. Clark Russell), 3 vols, Chatto & Windus 1890. Vol I ch. I–XIV; Vol II ch. XV–XXVIII; Vol III ch. XXIX–XLII.

**Vol I**
- Ch I "Down Channel": Countess Ida (Indiaman, bound Bombay) leaves Gravesend 4am, off South Foreland 8:30pm, Sept night. Narrator Laurence Dugdale (ex-midshipman, 2 yrs at sea, 6 yrs before). Chief mate Mr. Prance; second mate Mr. Cocker; Capt. Keeling (~60, white hair, "small sort of Commodore Dance"). Colonel Bannister (Indian army, fiery, wife with Roman nose). Dr. Hemmeridge (ship surgeon). Peter Hemskirk (Dutch, Bombay manager). Hon. Stephen Colledge (son of Lord Sandown, cabin-mate, drinks brandy, engaged to Fanny Crawley, daughter of Sir John Crawley). Captain's steward Handcock.
- Ch II "The French Lugger": Countess Ida runs down a French lugger (Boulogne); ~17–18 drowned; survivors (captain a leathery little man, red nightcap) taken off by cutter from a frigate; Miss Louise Temple (aunt Mrs. Radcliffe; dark eyes; "Thanks for the story"). Colonel Bannister's wife. Mr. Fairthorne (lisping Civil Service), Greenhew, Riley, Emmett (painter), Johnson (journalist), Mr. Adams (lawyer), Mr. Hodder, Saunders (dwarf pharmacist), Mrs. Joliffe, Hudson (Miss Constance Hudson, golden-haired), Trevor, Brookes.
- Ch III: fellow passengers at breakfast; Mr. Cocker and Captain's remarks; monkeys rule; sailor Crabb (one eye, hare-lip, carroty hair).
- Ch IV "Louise Temple": Louise's beauty; Mrs. Radcliffe; Louise's father Sir Conyers Temple; mother paralysed; uncle in India. Colledge flirts; Dugdale snubbed.
- Ch V "A Mysterious Voice": voice on topsail yard; sailor lied; parrot Prince (Chinaman John) escaped.
- Ch VI "We Lose a Man": Crabb dying; Mr. Smallridge (boatswain, silver pipe). Colledge's engagement revealed (Fanny Crawley). Johnson's wager.
- Ch VII "A Sea Funeral": Crabb buried; hammock floats; Dugdale and Louise on poop; Colonel accuses Hemmeridge of smallpox.
- Ch VIII "A Strange Cargo": wreck of schooner with monkeys; shot from Keeling's guns.
- Ch IX "A Secret Blow": helmsman Simpson struck down; meteorolite (Saunders). Greenhew/Riley fight.
- Ch X "Humours of an Indiaman": Greenhew/Riley fight; dances planned, fail.
- Ch XI "A Strange Sail": brig (privateer?) of ~260 tons; Mrs. Joliffe; Louise shoots parasol; Johnson/Emmett cowardice.
- Ch XII "A Storm of Wind": brig struck by lightning, on fire; Louise hangs from yard-of-hencoop; Dugdale rescues her.
- Ch XIII "Fire!": storm; Mrs Hudson fits; fire in hold forward; Crabb found alive in hold (faked death via potion "morion").
- Ch XIV "Crabb": Crabb sees; fire blankets; Hemmeridge suspected; Saunders's cabin dispute.

**Vol II**
- Ch XV "A Singular Plot": Keeling interrogates Crabb, Willett (sailmaker), Bobbins; Hemmeridge resigns; Saunders identifies drug "morion" (mandragora).
- Ch XVI "We Sight a Wreck": wreck of the brig; man-of-war *Magicienne* (Sir Edward Panton, cousin of Colledge); Lieutenant; invitation for Louise and Dugdale and Colledge.
- Ch XVII "The Magicienne": visit to corvette; dead Spaniard in wreck round-house ("Aspirante" name); Burgundy; cutter lieutenant falls overboard; fog.
- Ch XVIII "Adrift": Dugdale and Louise left on wreck; Colledge and crew in cutter; Dugdale tosses corpse overboard.
- Ch XIX "Night": night on wreck; Louise, wine, candle.
- Ch XX "I Search the Wreck": Louise alone with Dugdale; rain; buckets; rats; ship's bell.
- Ch XXI "We Sight a Sail": Dugdale makes signal fire, foresail; barque sighted.
- Ch XXII "The Lady Blanche": barque *Lady Blanche* (Captain John Braine, eyes like ebony, Mr. Lush carpenter/second mate, Wilkins steward, Joe Wetherly); takes them aboard; wreck blows up.
- Ch XXIII "Captain Braine": Braine's cabin, treasure secret; Mr. Chicken dead (prior mate).
- Ch XXIV "The Crew of the Barque": Joe Wetherly ("Joe Weatherly" misspell) messages; Louise & Dugdale.
- Ch XXV "I Keep a Lookout".
- Ch XXVI "I Am Questioned": Braine questions Dugdale on navigation; pistol found in Chicken's locker.
- Ch XXVII "The Brig's Longboat": Spanish longboat with pirates; Joe Wetherly's hurled marlinespike saves them.
- Ch XXVIII "I Question Wetherly".

**Vol III**
- Ch XXIX "Captain Begins a Story": Braine's 1831 story: ship *Ocean Monarch*, *Rosario*; gold of ~£200,000 buried on uncharted island, lat 33°6'S long 120°3'W; oath on Bible.
- Ch XXX "Captain Makes a Proposal": treasure chart; Dugdale agrees on pretence; Wilkins overheard.
- Ch XXXI "Form of Agreement": documents signed; Louise hides rings; Lush hostile.
- Ch XXXII "A Tragedy": Braine suicide (shot); body buried by Lush.
- Ch XXXIII "Carpenter Calls a Council": Lush and crew demand Dugdale navigate to island.
- Ch XXXIV "I Assent"; Ch XXXV "My Captaincy"; Ch XXXVI "I Converse with Wetherly"; Ch XXXVII "Cape Horn" (Maria Jane Taylor, whaler; Prussian/Dutch sails); Ch XXXVIII "Land!" (Lady Blanche anchored at island); Ch XXXIX "The Island" (dig for gold; Lush; Wilkins; Woodward); Ch XL "I Escape" (Dugdale swims to ship); Ch XLI "We Sail Away" (Forrest shot by Louise, seemingly in self-defence); Ch XLII "Conclusion": Peruvian brig; Valparaiso; *Greyhound* home; Lady Temple dies on news of Louise's loss; Louise inherits; Dugdale marries Louise; Lush tried for murder of Woodward, transported 10 years; Braine's treasure unfound.

---

## BOOK 2 — "Morley Ashton: A Story of the Sea" (James Grant), 3 vols, Tinsley 1876. Vol I ch. I–XXVII; Vol II ch. I–XXV; Vol III ch. (see below, text ended with Vol II ch XXV "Cabin Attacked"; Vol III text not provided in the excerpt—the excerpt includes vol.1 and vol.2 ending only, then "End of Vol II" and Vol III boilerplate ending "End of Project Gutenberg's Morley Ashton, Volume 3").

**Vol I (BOOK 2)**
- Ch I "Blind Goddess": Morley Ashton (Liverpool agent on Bonny River, West Africa; 3 years; malaria) returns at Acton-Rennel; meets Ethel Basset (~20) at Cherrywood Hill near Acton Chase; split sixpence; father Scriven Basset (ex-barrister, judge appt. Isle of France); sister Rose (18); Ethel's mother dead (grave under old yew, Acton church). Captain Bartelot (Tom, *Rattler*, Liverpool) cured him.
- Ch II "Laurel Lodge": house description; Mr. Basset; Captain Cramply Hawkshaw (self-styled, Texan Partisan Rangers, son of Tom Hawkshaw of Lincoln's Inn, rival) introduced; nugget ring with green stone.
- Ch III "Cramply Hawkshaw": Hawkshaw described (sinister, tarboosh, Spanish sash).
- Ch IV "Rivalry": walks; shamble-oak; Lucy Page; Hawkshaw's lasso anecdote.
- Ch V "Suspicion": Barradas story (Zuares and Pedro Barradas; Zuares kills his mother in the Barranca Secca near Orizaba, Mexico); Morley suspicious; Ethel gives ring back to Morley to return.
- Ch VI "For the Last Time": passage booked on *Hermione* (London, 500 tons, Captain John Phillips) to Isle of France; church farewell.
- Ch VII "The Rejection": Hawkshaw proposes to Ethel at Acton Chase; rejected; "Curse her!"
- Ch VIII "Morley and Hawkshaw": at Acton Chine (chasm ~400 ft); Hawkshaw pushes Morley over; Morley cries "Ethel!"
- Ch IX "Alarm": Hawkshaw returns alone; search; gloves, hat found.
- Ch X "Poor Ethel"; Ch XI "Darkness made Light" (Hawkshaw returns ring to himself); Ch XII "On board the good ship Hermione": Mr. Basset, Hawkshaw, Ethel, Rose, Nance Folgate (nurse) sail; Mate Manfredi (Italian); Dr. Leslie Heriot (Scot); Mate Samuel Quail; Foster second mate.
- Ch XIII "Acton Chine": Morley survives on ledge; rescued by *Princess* (Tom Bartelot's ship; mate Bill Morrison, Scot; Noah Gawthrop, old seaman).
- Ch XIV "The Rescue"; Ch XV "An Old Shipmate"; Ch XVI "Under the Tropic of Capricorn"; Ch XVII "Second Hearing" (Morrison's stories); Ch XVIII "Rio de Janeiro".
- Ch XIX "Ethel amid the Atlantic Isles" (Canaries Teguise; Pedro & Zuares Barradas on *Hermione*; Hawkshaw shaves beard); Ch XX "Moonlight on the Sea" (Rose and Heriot); Ch XXI "Story of a Brave Boy" (Manfredi's brother Attilio shot by Austrians at Pistoja, 1850); Ch XXII "Zuares and the Shark"; Ch XXIII "Hawkshaw's Old Friends" (Barradas blackmail; Hawkshaw's watch taken; Morley's corpse seen sinking — Hawkshaw's shock); Ch XXIV "Up Anchor" (Morley at Rio); Ch XXV "Suspicious Sail"; Ch XXVI "Strange Island" (Tristan/Hermit's Isle); Ch XXVII "The Hermit" (Pedro Zuares Miguel de Barradas hermit; manuscript confession of Mariquita Escudero, sons Pedro and Zuares).

**Vol II (BOOK 2)**
- Ch I "Mariquita Escudero" (full confession text; Pedro killed Juan Escudero; Mariquita's death).
- Ch II "Crew of *Hermione* Discontented" (Sharkey vs Manfredi; Manfredi strikes him with marlinespike).
- Ch III "Rose and Dr. Heriot" (engagement; ring).
- Ch IV "Man Overboard" (Manfredi lost; Sharkey suspected; Joe the steward witnesses).
- Ch V "The Livid Face" (face at porthole).
- Ch VI "Doctor Overheard in Forecastle Bunks" (mutineer plans; dice; Calabar beans).
- Ch VII "Measures for Defence" (barricade; Basset guards).
- Ch VIII "Sail to Windward" (*Princess* wreck follows; storm); Ch IX "Storm" (*Princess* dismasted); Ch X "Four Castaways" (Bartelot, Morley, Morrison, Noah on raft; Prussian barque *Einicheit* refuses); Ch XI "Captain Hawkshaw Makes a Discovery to Leeward"; Ch XII "Dr. Heriot's Patients" (castaways rescued by *Hermione*); Ch XIII "Hawkshaw's Troubles"; Ch XIV "Hawkshaw Turns Nurse" (Hawkshaw tries to strangle Morley); Ch XV "Biter Bitten" (Noah bites Hawkshaw's hand); Ch XVI "Dread"; Ch XVII "Unmasked"; Ch XVIII "Expulsion"; Ch XIX "The Meeting" (Ethel & Morley reunited); Ch XX "Corpse-Light"; Ch XXI "Out of Scylla"; Ch XXII "Four Bells in Dog-Watch"; Ch XXIII "Crisis at Last" (mutiny; Lush/Badger/Sharkey); Ch XXIV "Ship Broached To" (Joe killed; Mr. Quail killed; Hermione cut to pieces); Ch XXV "Cabin Attacked" (carronade fired with nails; Quail's corpse).

**Vol III (BOOK 2)** — text not included in the provided excerpt beyond Vol II's end (Vol III chapters follow in the original as Ch I "Sail Ho!" etc.; the excerpt does not contain Vol III body text).
